pages.title: Balloons and Lift
pages.text:
[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **Key points**

- [#](FFFFFF)[#]() **Hot air or steam** in sealed envelopes lifts the ship. More volume, more lift.
- Envelopes must be **airtight**.
- Lift weakens with altitude; a ship settles where lift equals weight.
- **Levitite** keeps a ship afloat but can't gain height alone.
Envelope blocks enclose a volume. Fill it with hot air or steam and it pulls the ship up. A bigger sealed volume gives the burners more lift to work with.

pages.title: Hot Air Envelope
pages.text: Must be airtight. Blocks inside shrink the volume. Dye them. Shafts can be [#](7A3C9A)[encased](entry://glossary/encased)[#]() in envelope blocks to stay sealed.

pages.title: Hot Air Burner
pages.text: Redstone fills the balloon above from the top down. Set the maximum output in its [#](7A3C9A)[panel](entry://glossary/value_panel)[#](). Several burners can feed one balloon. It burns no fuel: redstone alone runs it.

pages.title: Steam Vent
pages.text: Lift from steam instead. Like a Steam Engine it needs heat, water and [#](7A3C9A)[boiler](entry://glossary/boiler)[#]() space. See [#](2E5AAC)[Heat](entry://create_basics/heat)[#]() in the Create basics.

pages.title: Altitude and air
pages.text: Lift weakens as altitude rises, so a ship settles where lift and weight balance. Changing lift changes altitude. The Altitude Sensor outputs a redstone signal for height and, with [#](2E5AAC)[goggles](entry://create_basics/tools_wrench)[#](), shows air pressure. Other worlds have very different air: see [#](2E5AAC)[Planets](entry://space/planets)[#]().

pages.title: Speed and drag
pages.text:
Every envelope block drags as the ship moves, about as much as three blocks' worth of its weight, so an envelope bigger than the load needs makes it slower. Size it to the weight with room to climb: each m3 of hot air holds up about 1.5 mass low down, less higher up.\
\
Push level with the middle of the envelope: propellers low under it tip the nose up at speed.

pages.title: A whole airship
pages.text: [#](FFFFFF)[#]() **In depth.** How the envelope, gondola, engines, propellers and fins of an airship fit together, with a hauling blimp that cruises at about 9 blocks a second: [#](2E5AAC)[Designing Aircraft](entry://flight/aircraft_design)[#]().

pages.title: Levitite Blend
pages.text: A fluid from heated [#](7A3C9A)[mixing](entry://glossary/mixing)[#]() of End Stone Powder, zinc nuggets and water. Heat sets it into solid Levitite.

pages.title: Levitite
pages.text:
Keeps a ship afloat but **cannot gain height alone**; you need other forces. It resists slow motion strongly and less so at speed.\
\
Each block holds up 10 kpg of ship, itself included (Jade shows block weights). A heavier ship sinks slowly. Keep it level with the weight: a heavy stack on top of a small Levitite row tips over and falls.

pages.title: Where it comes from
pages.text: [#](FFFFFF)[#]() **In depth.** End Stone Powder comes from crushing End Stone. Sky whale bone dust can replace it. Pearlescent Levitite is a pink variant of the same crystal. Certain blocks break when Levitite sets, which is useful for casting molds.
